name.text: EOT_Q41: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following practical instructions did John the Baptist give to demonstrate true repentance in Luke 3? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: Luke 3:11-14 commands sharing extra clothing and food, professional honesty in tax collection, and contentment and non-violence in military service.

name.text: EOT_Q42: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following events occurred on the single fateful day of the Battle of Aphek? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: 1 Samuel 4:10-18 records all four tragic events taking place on the same catastrophic day.

name.text: EOT_Q43: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following promises were included in God's covenant with Abram in Genesis 12:2–3? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: God promised Abram a great nation, personal blessing, a great name, and universal blessing to all families of the earth. He was never promised the Egyptian throne.

name.text: EOT_Q44: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following honors were conferred upon Joseph when Pharaoh appointed him Prime Minister of Egypt? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: Pharaoh gave Joseph his signet ring, fine linen robes, a gold chain, and the second chariot (Genesis 41:42-43). Joseph was never commanded to worship idols.

name.text: EOT_Q45: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following virtues were demonstrated in the life and conduct of Ruth in Bethlehem? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: Ruth demonstrated sacrificial loyalty, humble hard work, and noble moral character (Ruth 1:16; 2:7; 3:11). She never demanded money from Naomi.

name.text: EOT_Q46: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each biblical figure with their specific confession or cry of repentance/obedience:

generalfeedback.text: David confessed after Nathan; Zacchaeus pledged restitution; Ruth made her covenant vow; and Joseph refused adultery.

name.text: EOT_Q47: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each place with its significance in the Second Term curriculum:

generalfeedback.text: Nineveh repented; Shiloh was the Tabernacle site; Moriah was the sacrifice mountain; and Bethlehem was the harvest field.

name.text: EOT_Q48: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each biblical character with their specific role or event:

generalfeedback.text: Nathan convicted David; John preached in the wilderness; Eli was the passive father; and Boaz was the kinsman-redeemer.

name.text: EOT_Q49: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each Hebrew or theological term with its precise biblical meaning:

generalfeedback.text: Metanoia is repentance; Ichabod is departed glory; Jehovah Jireh is God's provision; and Kinsman-Redeemer is family redeemer.

name.text: EOT_Q50: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each life event of Joseph with the corresponding stage of his service:

generalfeedback.text: Dothan was the pit; Potiphar's house was domestic management/purity; prison was dream interpretation/care; and palace was Prime Minister and grain administrator.
